lessons.title: Beginning again
lessons.objective: Learn that noticing wandering and returning is the practice, rather than a failure of the practice.

script_blocks.text: Welcome.
Take a moment to settle into a position that feels comfortable and awake.
Let the chair, floor, or surface beneath you take your weight.
Let your back be upright, without making it rigid.
Place your hands wherever they can rest without effort.
Let your shoulders drop, and allow your face to soften.
If it feels comfortable, you can close your eyes.
Or leave them slightly open, with a soft gaze resting on one place.
You can adjust your position at any point if your body needs to move.
Over the next few minutes, we will use the feeling of breathing as a place to rest attention.
There is nothing you need to force, and nowhere special to reach.
Begin with the clearest feeling of contact.
Feel the weight of your body, and the support beneath you.
Notice that breathing is already happening.
Choose one place where the breath is easiest to feel.
script_blocks.pause_instruction: For the next few moments, feel one breath from beginning to end. Then feel the next.

script_blocks.text: Sooner or later, attention will leave the breath.
It may move into a thought, a sound, a memory, or a plan.
That is expected.
The moment you realise it has wandered is a moment of awareness.
Acknowledge what took you away, without turning it into a problem.
script_blocks.pause_instruction: For the next part, stay with the breath. Each time you notice wandering, return to the next breath you can feel.

script_blocks.text: Each return is one small act of training.
You do not need to measure an improvement while you sit here.
script_blocks.pause_instruction: For a while, keep feeling the breath. Let each moment of noticing become a gentle return.

script_blocks.text: Now let the breath sit in a wider field.
Feel the whole body breathing.
Sounds may come and go.
Thoughts may form and dissolve.
Let all of that be present without following every movement.
script_blocks.pause_instruction: Stay with this wider field. Let breath, sound, and thought come and go. Return to the body whenever you are carried away.

script_blocks.text: For the next part, I will say less.
Let the practice become your own.
script_blocks.pause_instruction: For the next part, practise on your own. Rest with the breath. Notice wandering. Then begin again, gently and deliberately.

script_blocks.text: Now allow your attention to widen.
Notice the room, or the space around you.
Feel the whole body again.
You did not need a blank mind. You practised noticing, and choosing to return.
During the day, one ordinary breath can be enough to make that same movement again.

lessons.title: Walking with attention
lessons.objective: Bring attention into movement and contact.

script_blocks.text: Welcome.
Begin walking at a pace that feels natural and easy.
Let your arms hang loosely at your sides.
Or rest your hands wherever they feel comfortable.
Let your shoulders drop, and allow your face to soften.
Keep your gaze soft, resting somewhere ahead of you.
You can change your pace at any point if your body needs to.
Over the next few minutes, we will use the feeling of walking as a place to rest attention.
There is nothing you need to force, and nowhere special to reach.
Begin with the clearest feeling of contact.
Feel the ground meet each foot, step after step.
Feel the weight move from one foot to the other.
Notice the rhythm of your steps.
Choose one place in the walking where the contact is easiest to feel.
script_blocks.pause_instruction: For the next few moments, feel each step from beginning to end. Then feel the next.

script_blocks.text: Sooner or later, attention will leave the walking.
It may move into a thought, a sound, a memory, or a plan.
That is expected.
The moment you realise it has wandered is a moment of awareness.
Acknowledge what took you away, without turning it into a problem.
script_blocks.pause_instruction: For the next part, stay with the walking. Each time you notice wandering, return to the next step you can feel.

script_blocks.text: Each return is one small act of training.
You do not need to measure an improvement while you walk.
script_blocks.pause_instruction: For a while, keep feeling each step. Let each moment of noticing become a gentle return.

script_blocks.text: Now let the walking rest in a wider field.
Feel the whole body moving as you walk.
Feel the air on your skin.
Sounds may come and go.
Thoughts may form and dissolve.
Let all of that be present without following every movement.
script_blocks.pause_instruction: Stay with this wider field. Let step, sound, and thought come and go. Return to the body whenever you are carried away.

script_blocks.text: For the next part, I will say less.
Let the practice become your own.
script_blocks.pause_instruction: For the next part, practise on your own. Rest with the walking. Notice wandering. Then begin again, gently and deliberately.

script_blocks.text: Now allow your attention to widen.
Notice the space around you.
Feel the whole body again.
You did not need a blank mind. You practised noticing, and choosing to return.
During the day, one ordinary step can be enough to make that same movement again.
